concepts.def: Das Heilige 1917 describes mysterium tremendum et fascinans; non-rational core of religion.
Varieties of Religious Experience 1902 Gifford Lectures; four marks of mystical experience: ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity.
Negative theology of Pseudo-Dionysius c.500 CE and Meister Eckhart (d.1328); knows God by what God is not.
Rabia of Basra (d.801) introduced divine love; al-Hallaj (executed 922) declared 'Ana al-Haqq'; Rumi (d.1273) and Ibn Arabi (d.1240).
Teresa of Avila (d.1582) Interior Castle, John of the Cross (d.1591) Dark Night, Julian of Norwich (d.c.1416) Revelations.
Advaita non-dualism of Shankara (788-820); identifies Atman with Brahman; samadhi as direct realisation.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Religious Experience — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious Experience brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religious Experience.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
